scope: Read-only identity review of the four live research files; descriptive metadata and cached author descriptions, not gameplay verification

manually_adjudicated_candidates.reason: Different authors. First is endless generated dungeon soul collection; Lost Souls (and Paperwork) is hell paperwork rescue with six managed stats. Matching short title alone is not same-game evidence.
BulletBoi has three dungeons and tap-dodge/hold-charge. Bullet Boy has health-cost bullet absorption, gravitational pull and ten-wave NecroKing endpoint. Different authors and distinct rules.
Fair Squares upgrades the enemy whenever the player upgrades. Fair and Square specifies ten escalating waves and a last-wave boss. Different authors; name resemblance is insufficient.
Slimecide has a colonist fighting slime waves. Slime Crime is a slime with mutually exclusive move/shoot/harvest actions. Distinct authors, protagonists and loops.

Same author but separate named projects: Creature Survivors author page says Unity over 1.5 months, five characters, seventeen weapons and eight evolutions; Pixel Arena Survivors says Godot over three weeks, ten-minute arena then boss. Neither reviewed page declares remake or port.

Same studio does not establish duplicate: Die Recompile persists destruction through replacement clones; Gaunt Valkyr describes three characters and weapon-mod behavior. Reviewed text does not identify the pages as versions of one game.

Threadbound rotates movement and makes shooting slow the player; floor zones change attacks. Threadborne is fifteen-minute survival with magic cards added by level-ups and chests. Different authors, titles and rule structure.
Bullet Bunny has a five-hundred-second endpoint with four guns and six gems; Bullet Boy absorbs bullets by spending health and has a ten-wave NecroKing endpoint. Only generic Bullet name resembles.

version_family_watchlist.reason: Counted author page explicitly calls itself the old Weekly Jam prototype and links an updated demo under the second author. Count the family once if both appear.
Counted author page explicitly calls this a revamp and links the game-jam original. Count the family once if both appear.
Author states Deluxe includes the same free core game plus DLC. Do not count an eventual base-game page twice.
Help! author explicitly says it became Colt Canyon. Treat as one design family for a conservative unique-game threshold if a separate Colt Canyon record appears.

Explicit derivative mod, not an alias. It contains its own six-character/mutation system; disclose derivation. Conservative gate may exclude mods but should not silently relabel it as base-game research.

limitations: Author identity and mechanics can disprove superficial title matches, but no universal game-ID exists on itch.io. Files still being updated must be re-read. A linked sequel is not automatically the same game; a linked updated demo generally is.
